stem: Priya's mother makes a glass of nimbu pani (lemon water) by stirring lemon juice, sugar and salt into water until everything dissolves. Priya looks at the glass and cannot see the sugar, salt or lemon juice separately. How should Priya classify this mixture, and why?

options.text: Uniform mixture, because the components are spread evenly throughout and cannot be seen separately
Non-uniform mixture, because it contains more than one substance mixed together
Uniform mixture, because the lemon juice gives it one colour that can be seen
Non-uniform mixture, because the sugar is heavier than water and settles down

teacher.key_rationale: A fully dissolved solution like nimbu pani is a uniform (homogeneous) mixture: components are evenly distributed and cannot be distinguished even with a microscope. B is the trap for a student who drops the 'evenly spread' condition and assumes that having more than one substance automatically makes a mixture non-uniform. C misuses appearance of colour as the criterion. D is factually wrong for a dissolved solution.
